title: Whether those sides were meant as hits, and who approached her to record
summary: She says it was just a date, not a hit-seeking one, and she was approached by different people after coming off the road.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Do you have -- how do you feel about recording those songs? You said you were looking for a hit song. Did you think that any of these might've been --

I wasn't looking -- This was just a date. Naturally, it came out, you know, with my name on the label, but it was more than likely Cedric Wallace's date. He probably made the arrangements, you know. And they might've hoped for the best. Because these were all original songs. I mean they were new! I don't think anybody has ever recorded these. They weren't bad songs. They sound better today to me now than they did when I recorded them. But it was -- in my estimation, it was the first attempt at trying to be commercial, if you want to put it that way.

Did they sell particularly well compared to --

No, I don't think so. I really don't think so. I never heard him. I just did the date and that was the end of that. I think my particular reason for doing them was because I just wanted something out there on record. But there was no way to -- we had no way of exploiting these songs, see. If you don't have a means to get them out to the general public so that they can go out and buy them, they're just there. You just make records and they're just there. I wasn't in a position to do anything about it. In fact, at that time I wouldn't have known how to go about it -- exploiting it. And by this time, I wasn't under management to nobody. I was on my own, and I didn't have access to the industry or the larger powers that be. So I was pretty much on my own.

And this is, of course, as a result of my having come off the road and went into this club. I mean, I acutally turned down a lot of engagements and a lot of work, because I had been travelling a long time, I was tired; and I had this steady job, so to speak, and I wasn't out there in the limelight. I was in a club more or less excluded.
And this date came up -- and some of the other ones a little later which we will discuss -- they came up, and we just did them to be making recordings.

I was approached mainly by the different people here. You know, like the different -- In this particular case, it was Joe Davis. You know, they were taking a chance. Even the next set, you know, made a -- I don't know -- as an art piece, or something like that. I don't know. But it was sort of a strange period at that time.
